observations: Three photos show a gasoline engine on a dirty ground, surrounded by people and other engine parts.
The engine has a complex layout with many hoses, belts, and components, including a visible intake manifold and turbocharger.
Photo 0 shows the front of the engine with the timing cover and pulleys; a small white label is visible but unreadable.
Photo 1 shows the top and side of the engine with the intake manifold, throttle body, and various sensors and connectors.
Photo 2 shows the rear and side of the engine with the turbocharger, exhaust manifold, and EGR system.
The engine appears to be from a modern vehicle, likely a turbocharged inline-4 or V6, given the complexity and presence of a turbocharger.
There is no visible branding or model number on any part of the engine in any photo.
The engine is dirty, with grime and oil residue, consistent with 'fairly used' but not necessarily indicating poor condition.
No signs of major damage or catastrophic failure are visible, but internal condition is unknown.

The engine has a typical gasoline engine layout with spark plug wires, throttle body, and fuel rail (visible in photo 1).
Horsepower cannot be determined from visual inspection alone; requires model and specifications.
Performance cannot be assessed without knowing the model, tuning, or dyno data.

Video of the engine running, showing smooth operation and no smoke or knocking.
Photo of the engine's VIN or vehicle identification tag if available.
response.reason: The engine cannot be identified by brand or model, and key claims (Land Rover, high performance, like new) are unverified or contradicted. Internal condition and provenance are unknown, which affects pricing. Proof is needed to determine the correct identity and condition.
